title: Senior AI Governance Counsel
description: This is Adyen Adyen provides payments, data, and financial products in a single solution for customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, and Microsoft - making us the financial technology platform of choice. At Adyen, everything we do is engineered for ambition.  For our teams, we create an environment with opportunities for our people to succeed, backed by the culture and support to ensure they are enabled to truly own their careers. We are motivated individuals who tackle unique technical challenges at scale and solve them as a team. Together, we deliver innovative and ethical solutions that help businesses achieve their ambitions faster. The Role We are looking for a Senior AI Governance Counsel to join our Global DPO Office and help build, roll out, and operate Adyen's enterprise AI governance framework. Sitting within the group that owns our global privacy program and AI governance, and supports incident response and management as well as data governance, you will be the driving force in shaping our strong foundations into a consistent, enterprise-wide AI governance program that scales with Adyen's ambitions - helping the business innovate boldly and responsibly with AI. This is a builder role. You will translate the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, GDPR, the CCPA/CPRA, and emerging global AI and privacy requirements into pragmatic policies, standards, and assessment workflows - and partner with Enterprise Risk, Security, Product, Compliance, Legal, Regulatory and Engineering to make them real. You will have a particular focus on generative and agentic AI use cases, and on giving first-line teams the parameters and tooling they need to evaluate their own models and outcomes. What You'll Do Help build, roll out, and embed Adyen's enterprise-wide AI governance framework, policies, and standards, driving consistency as AI adoption scales across the business. Design and operationalize AI risk and impact assessments across the AI lifecycle - from intake and risk classification through deployment, monitoring, and decommissioning - with particular focus on generative and agentic AI use cases. Interpret the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and other applicable AI laws across Adyen's global footprint, and translate them into practical policies, playbooks, and procedures for first-line teams. Support the teams that maintain Adyen's AI inventories by defining governance parameters and requirements for cataloguing and risk-classifying AI tools and use cases.  Develop enterprise guidance and a consistent approach for evaluating AI systems, covering performance, fairness, and explainability expectations appropriate to each use case's risk profile. Design simple, proportionate, risk-tiered processes and “green paths” that make responsible AI the easy path for fast-moving teams - using clear risk tiers and practical incentives so the compliant route is also the most convenient one. Translate model-evaluation techniques - including fairness, bias, and adversarial (red-teaming) testing - into clear procedures that technology teams can apply to their own models and tools. Partner with Enterprise Risk, Security, Product, Compliance, Legal, Regulatory, and Engineering to run the AI governance program and align on controls, escalation, and human-oversight protocols. Advise on privacy considerations across the AI lifecycle, coordinating with the wider DPO Office on the interaction between AI assessments and data protection. Design and deliver AI governance training and promote AI literacy and a culture of responsible, accountable AI use. Monitor global AI and privacy developments and translate them into proportionate governance requirements, supporting responses to audit, regulatory, and client inquiries. Who You Are Core Expertise: 7+ Years in AI Governance/Privacy: Proven background building, deploying, and managing global AI or privacy governance programs, ideally within regulated, multi-jurisdictional environments Legal / Risk Qualification: Qualified lawyer or governance professional with substantial experience in AI governance, privacy, or technology risk. (US jurisdiction admission is a plus) Regulated Sector Background: Prior experience in payments, financial services, or other heavily regulated industries is preferred. Technical Knowledge: AI Frameworks & Privacy Laws: Solid working knowledge of the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO/IEC 42001, along with global privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) Generative & Agentic AI Experience: Familiarity with LLMs, autonomy levels, human-in-the-loop design, and tool/action permissioning Model Evaluation & Testing: Understanding of model evaluation techniques including fairness, bias, drift, performance, explainability, and red teaming, and the ability to translate them into practical policies. Leadership & Collaboration Regulatory Translator: Skilled at converting complex, fast-evolving AI regulations into practical, business

title: Senior Counsel, Product & Privacy
description: The Team Stability AI’s Legal team works on exciting cutting edge questions of law.  You’ll join Legal as the main legal partner to our product, research, and engineering organizations. Day to day, you’ll work with product managers, engineers, researchers, release management, security and infosec, and our commercial team on products across audio, image, video, and 3D. We’re building toward a consistent, documented legal review for every data and product release, and a privacy program that keeps up with a growing global business. The Work Lead product and privacy counseling for multiple generative AI product teams. You’ll learn our models, products, and development processes well enough to spot legal, security, and ethical risks early and recommend practical ways to handle them. Build and run the policies, processes, and documentation that govern data and product releases. You’ll work with product, engineering, release management, and security. Advance our global privacy and data security compliance program, and partner with infosec on incident response and data security practices. Advise on copyright across the model lifecycle: licensing and use of training datasets, rights in generative output, and content-hosting obligations such as the DMCA and Article 17 of the EU Copyright Directive. Track global AI regulation, such as the EU AI Act, and help product teams put ethics and safety initiatives into practice. You’ll also guide compliance with trade rules, including US export controls and the Trade Agreements Act. Equip the commercial team to understand our technology, licensing frameworks, and IP strategy so they can answer customer questions with confidence. What You Bring Qualifications JD from an accredited law school and active bar membership in good standing. Experience 10+ years of experience as an attorney, with a focus on technology product counseling, privacy, and intellectual property. In-house experience as a product counselor at a technology company. Experience building and maintaining data privacy compliance programs. Experience working with cross-functional teams and managing multiple priorities. Skills & Expertise Deep understanding of data privacy law (such as GDPR and CCPA), emerging AI law (such as the EU AI Act), and consumer protection law. A passion for understanding how AI technology works, and the ability to turn an engineer’s technical explanation into concrete legal mitigations and contract provisions. A practical approach to commercially reasonable risk mitigation when both the law and the business are uncertain. Excellent analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to distill complex legal concepts into clear, actionable guidance for non-legal stakeholders. A proactive mindset for identifying and addressing legal risks. The ability to address problems creatively and with an open mind. The ability to work both independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, with the flexibility to adapt as priorities change. The ability to build relationships and collaborate with internal clients. A high level of integrity, professionalism, and attention to detail. An inquisitive attitude focused on problem solving and consensus-building. Additional Strengths An understanding of how data is used to train generative AI models, and the risks and opportunities that come with it. Experience with open source, data, or source-available licensing, and with open source communities. Experience drafting and updating terms of service and privacy policies for a global technology company, or privacy certifications such as CIPP/US or CIPP/E. Benefits & Compensation A remote-first company with teammates across multiple countries who bring diverse perspectives, and flexibility built into how we collaborate. Health coverage for you and your family. Choose from PPO and HMO plans, including select plans where Stability AI covers 100% of premiums for you and your eligible dependents. HSA and FSA accounts to set aside pre-tax dollars for healthcare and other eligible expenses. Company-paid life insurance, with the option to add voluntary coverage for yourself, your spouse, and your children. Short- and long-term disability coverage, to protect part of your income if illness or injury keeps you from working. 401(k) with company match of up to 4%. Paid parental leave to support you as your family grows. Flexible paid time off, plus paid company holidays. The equipment you need to do your best work, provided by Stability AI. At Stability AI, we aim to pay fairly and competitively, and we believe you should know what a role pays before you invest time in getting to know us. The annual base salary range for this role is $200,000 - $270,000 USD. It reflects our good-faith expectation for the role as posted and applies to candidates hired within the United States. Where you fall within that range depends on the depth and relevance of your experience, your skills

title: Head of Internal Audit
description: About Faire Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. Independent retailers around the globe collectively represent a multi-hundred-billion-dollar wholesale market that has historically been fragmented and offline. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive. We’re looking for smart, resourceful and passionate people to join us as we power the shop local movement. If you believe in community, come join ours. About this role We're looking for a Head of Internal Audit to build Faire's Internal Audit function and lead our SOX (financial controls) program as we prepare for public company requirements. You’ll partner with process owners across the company to make sure our key controls are well designed, operating effectively, and supported by complete and accurate data. This role owns the audit plan, is an independent voice on risk and controls, and partners closely with the Audit Committee. You'll inherit a small SOX team and shape how it's structured as Internal Audit grows, with scope that may expand into areas like enterprise risk management. You'll also help govern how Faire builds and uses AI, and use data and AI to make audit faster and more continuous. As Finance and the business rebuild workflows around AI, you’ll make sure those workflows are SOX compliant by design: advising on controls throughout the build process, setting the standard for evidence and review, and giving the Audit Committee and our external auditor confidence in the results. You understand our technology environment, have built or scaled an audit function at a fast-growing tech company, and are ready to roll up your sleeves. You see the Internal Audit function as a partner to the business, not a checkpoint. This role reports to the CAO, with a functional reporting line to the CFO and the Audit Committee of the Board. What you’ll do  Build and lead Faire's Internal Audit function, including the audit plan, team, and outside partners Lead our SOX team and own the SOX program, including readiness for our first external audit of internal controls Review controls over our technology: cloud, software changes, system access, data, and cybersecurity Provide independent assurance over how Faire builds and uses AI, including model errors, bias, and privacy Modernize audit with data analytics, automation, and responsible AI to test more and monitor continuously Give the Audit Committee and executives a clear, candid view of risk and control health Partner with Finance, Legal, Security, Privacy, and Engineering to advise on controls early for new products, systems, and expansion Track issues to closure and push for root-cause fixes Hire, coach, and develop the team and manage outside audit partners Take on special projects, analysis, and reporting as needed Qualifications Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, information systems, or a related field, plus at least one of CPA, CIA, CISA, or CISSP 12+ years in audit and risk, including 6+ reviewing IT and financial controls and 3+ leading teams Deep SOX experience, including IPO readiness or first-year external auditor review of internal controls Strong understanding of the technology environment, including IT controls, cloud, data, and cybersecurity Working knowledge of AI risk and governance, including generative and agentic AI, and experience using AI or analytics in audit Knowledge of US GAAP, COSO, PCAOB, and IIA standards Experience presenting to Audit Committees, boards, and senior executives Experience selecting audit and risk technology Experience building an internal audit function at a tech company; hyper-growth or marketplace experience is a plus Strong communicator with sound judgment in ambiguous situations Resourceful and not afraid to roll up your sleeves Salary range: San Francisco: The salary range for this role is $200,000 - $275,000 per year. Security engineering and risk management: Strong expertise across Identity and Access Management (IAM), endpoint protection, application security and network security, including threat modelling, security risk assessments and the definition of appropriate remediation strategies. DevSecOps and secure delivery: Experience embedding security controls into the software development lifecycle, applying DevSecOps principles and collaborating with engineering teams to support secure software and infrastructure delivery. Bonus Points For Relevant professional certifications, including CISSP, CISM, TOGAF or recognised cloud security certifications. Experience defining AI security architectures, responsible AI governance frameworks, security guardrails or controls for AI-enabled systems, including Generative AI and Agentic AI, within regulated environments. Hands-on experience with security tooling, including Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms, firewalls and Identity and Access Management solutions. Experience supporting regulatory compliance requirements, including GDPR and PCI-DSS, particularly within financial services or other regulated industries. Familiarity with programming languages such as Python, Java or C++, with the ability to understand how software engineering practices influence security architecture and technical delivery. Access continuous learning, training and industry certifications. Be part of a team shaping the future of digital financial services. Help shape the future of digital transformation across financial services and energy. title: Head of Customer Experience & Trust
description: This role can be based in our Rotterdam HQ or in our Cergy office. We're on a mission to become the go-to destination for students across Europe to find a trusted home away from home. We make every step of the rental journey simple and seamless, so students can focus on what really matters: studying, exploring, and growing. With HousingAnywhere, Kamernet, and Studapart under our roof, we're Europe's largest student rental platform. You'll find us in Rotterdam, Paris, and Cergy, always guided by our four core values: Ownership, We are enablers, We are changemakers, and We are connectors. We're looking for a Head of Customer Experience & Trust to be the guardian of the tenant experience on our unified platform. As we consolidate the HousingAnywhere and Studapart operations teams, you will lead a multi-site support and trust organisation across Rotterdam and Cergy and own not just how we respond to our users, but the content, policies, and safeguards that shape their experience before they ever contact us. This covers listing moderation, fraud prevention and dispute handling. Use AI-based detection and moderation so we always display real content from real users, with human judgement on the final call. Own the cancellation flows: All cancellation assessment and resolution flows sit with you, including post-cancellation retention and relocation. Automate what’s simple and keep a human touch where tenants need it most. Protect our reputation: Protects the platform’s reputation on Trustpilot and Google, and acts on Voice of Customer insights from the Quality & Training Manager. Your profile Professional experience: 5+ years in customer operations, with 2+ years leading multi-team or multi-site support organisations, ideally in a marketplace, travel or high-volume consumer platform. Hands-on AI deployment: You have deployed an AI support agent in production, not just piloted one. You can show how you improved its resolution rate and quality over time. Knowledge and content ownership: You have shaped T&Cs, help content or service policies with Legal and Product. You write rules that both people and AI can follow. Trust & safety literacy : You have owned or worked hands-on with moderation, fraud prevention and dispute resolution, and can balance protection with conversion. Data-driven: You run on SLAs, CSAT, automation and cancellation metrics. You know how to hold quality through seasonal peaks. Peak and partner management: You have prepared support teams for seasonal peaks, and have selected and managed BPO partners, holding them to the same quality standard as your own team. Change leadership: You lead through team leads and have taken a team through a change in roles driven by automation, keeping people engaged along the way. Responsible AI: You know where AI should stop and a human should take over. You are familiar with GDPR and EU AI Act transparency requirements for customer-facing AI. Languages: Fluent English required; French a strong plus. What's in it for you Position based in our Cergy office (hybrid working policy), with visits to HQ in Rotterdam.
